name: Malignant Germ Cell Tumor of the Corpus Uteri

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Malignant Germ Cell Tumors of the Corpus Uteri

criteria.description: Presence of malignant germ cell tumor histology in uterine corpus tissue biopsy
Positive immunohistochemical staining for germ cell tumor markers such as AFP, hCG, PLAP, and OCT3/4
Pelvic MRI or CT showing a mass localized to the corpus uteri with features suggestive of germ cell tumor
Elevated serum alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) or beta-human chorionic gonadotropin (β-hCG) levels

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of malignant germ cell tumor in uterine corpus tissue with positive immunohistochemical markers
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of metastatic germ cell tumors from other primary sites.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pelvic mass detected on physical examination

searchTerms: pain in lower abdomen or pelvis
low red blood cells from bleeding
anemia due to chronic blood loss

rare.symptomName: Lower extremity edema due to pelvic venous compression
searchTerms: lower limb edema due to vein compression

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to brain metastases
searchTerms: neurological problems due to brain metastases

laboratory: Anemia due to chronic blood loss
imaging: Pelvic MRI showing heterogeneous mass in corpus uteri
CT scan demonstrating uterine mass with possible local invasion
genetic: No specific germline mutations identified; somatic mutations may be present in tumor tissue
other: Histopathology revealing yolk sac tumor, dysgerminoma, or mixed germ cell tumor components
Immunohistochemical positivity for PLAP, OCT3/4, AFP, and hCG

distinguishingFeatures: Histology shows adenocarcinoma rather than germ cell tumor
Lack of germ cell tumor markers (AFP, hCG)
Primary tumor located in ovary rather than corpus uteri
Clinical history of ovarian germ cell tumor

redFlags: Severe abnormal uterine bleeding causing hemodynamic instability
Elevated serum AFP or β-hCG indicating aggressive tumor activity
references: Orphanet: Malignant germ cell tumor of the corpus uteri - ORPHA:213751
Kurman RJ, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs. 4th Edition. IARC; 2014.
Gadducci A, et al. Malignant germ cell tumors of the female genital tract: a review. Gynecol Oncol. 2019.
